provenance.description: CLIENT: explicitly supplied. RESEARCHED: evidenced, cite in evidenceRefs. INFERRED: concluded from established domain behaviour, rationale required. SYSTEM: the product cannot function without it. SECURITY: threat mitigation or access control. REGULATORY: required by law, policy, or platform rule. ASSUMED: nobody supplied it, a default was taken under the silence-is-consent rule — requires the assumption object.

assumption.description: Required when provenance is ASSUMED. Records the default taken so silence remains auditable.

question.description: The unanswered question this requirement rests on.

default.description: The decision taken in the absence of an answer.

costIfWrong.description: STRUCTURAL means dependent work is discarded rather than adjusted if the default is wrong.

upstream.description: Artifact IDs this requirement derives from. Changing any of them marks this STALE.

downstream.description: Artifact IDs derived from this requirement. Maintained by the traceability pass, not by hand.

priority.description: MUST_HAVE: the product is not worth shipping without it — if everything else shipped and this did not, nobody would use it. NICE_TO_HAVE: meaningfully better with it, but the product works and is worth using without it. POLISH: what separates a good product from one that merely works — does not change what the product does (onboarding, empty states, error copy, keyboard access, perceived speed, consistency). Polish is scheduled, never silently dropped; anything that changes what the product can do is a capability, not polish.
